allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.5 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dull green leaves, woolly beneath; pink flower spires.

appearance.organs.bloom.note: Its panicle drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c), its kind from its genus's inflorescence, by the rule at the flowering plants: a narrow cone of 20 short branches, each of 4 branches of 6 pink flowers, by eye, so that it is as dense as the floras say (the Flora of North America gives dense conic panicles 8 to 25 cm long and 3 to 6 cm wide, their height 2 to 4 times their width, and no count). Each flower is drawn about 4.5 mm across, its long pink stamens taken in: the flowers are 2 to 4 mm across and their stamens 2 to 3 times as long as the petals, which makes the panicle look fuzzy; the stamens are too small to draw. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five pink petals between five sepals on a floral cup, its long stamens and five free pistils, from the characters of its own, Rosaceae's and Spiraea's by the rules at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.bloom.inflorescence.ki.note: How PlantGen lays out an inflorescence, a choice of the model's (spec rework L1): the inflorescence characters set the cluster of any look a taxon draws as one (`"inflorescence": {}`), its kind, how many units it bears on each axis, its primary branches and how it holds itself. Sizes, stalks and spacing stay set by hand until programs size their organs from characters.

appearance.organs.bloom.shape.carpels.note: How PlantGen draws a flower, a choice of the model's (spec rework P5): the flower characters set a flower card's perianth, its parts, how they differ by place, how far the corolla is joined into a tube, a floral cup, where the ovary sits, a resupinate flower's turn, its stamens, staminodes and carpels and its spurs. The rules also set these fields in a season's flower and bud looks that draw a flower, unless set there by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a dense, thicket-forming shrub of many straight, upright stems with oblong leaves toothed near the tip and fluffy spires of deep pink flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.bud_base.note: Barthélémy and Caraglio (2007, read in excerpts): a basitonic shoot branches mostly from its proximal part.

generator.params.crown_height.note: What the broadleaf program's crown_height means: the top of the space the crown may fill, which rises with age at crown_rate toward it and never passes it, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest. Where that greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.leaves_per_node.note: What the words mean, as accounts of phyllotaxis such as Okabe and colleagues' use them: a spiral or two-ranked shoot bears one leaf at a node, a decussate one a pair and a whorled one three or more. A spiral turns about the golden angle (137.5 degrees) from node to node and two ranks half a turn; pairs and whorls alternate, each standing over the gaps of the one below, half the gap between its own leaves round (90 degrees for pairs). Three ranks turn a third of a turn, as their name says.

generator.params.long_share.note: Barthélémy and Caraglio (2007, read in excerpts): the buds that grow are concentrated toward one end of the annual shoot (acrotony, basitony) or in its middle (mesotony). How many is the model's choice: as many as the steps of vigour the shoot grew, so a shoot keeps the buds able to grow long that it had before it was cut into a growth unit, gathered at its tip or its foot, or twice as many reaching into its middle; the rest grow short shoots.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.params.short_share.note: Barthélémy and Caraglio (2007, read in excerpts) describe the buds of a growth unit grading along it, the most vigorous laterals at its favoured end; the buds farthest from it often never grow. How many grow short shoots is the model's choice: a third as many as may grow long ones, fitted so open-grown crowns hold the leaf area per crown area of the Urban Tree Database's trees (as many as the long ones gave an 80-year Oregon white oak 6.4 m² a m² against valley oaks' 1.9 to 5.3; none halved red alder's leaf area).

generator.params.terminal_bloom.note: A choice of the model's: a shoot that ends in flowers is carried on by the buds below them, so the crown forks; the chance a year, 0.35, is the maple program's, fitted to bigleaf maple, and half that where flowers may also sit beside the leaves.

generator.params.unit_nodes.note: Critchfield (1971, read in full) found a maple's long shoot about as long as its leaf pairs are many, each pair a few centimetres up the stem; so a shoot of the program's longest year's growth carries the taxon's shoot_leaves, and each of the program's internodes is cut into as many nodes as that takes. The internode the program grows by is a step of vigour, not a node. Corner's rules (Corner 1949) tie a twig's leaves to its spacing: the larger the leaves, the fewer and farther apart, so nodes are kept at least a quarter of the leaf card's length apart.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

generator.spreads.params.crown_height.note: What the broadleaf program's crown_height means: the top of the space the crown may fill, which rises with age at crown_rate toward it and never passes it, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest. Where that greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
